title: Type conversion: implicit, explicit and loss of precision

videos.script: Values of different types meet all the time, and something has to convert them. This lesson is about who does it, and what gets lost. {{widen}} Java converts by itself in one direction only, from a smaller type to a larger one. That can never overflow. It can still round, and you will watch an int lose its last digit on the way into a float. {{narrow}} The other direction needs a cast. A cast never fails. It always gives you a number, and sometimes the wrong one. {{promote}} Then expressions. Two bytes added together make an int. Seven divided by two is three. And a plus sign next to a string joins text instead of adding. {{parse}} Last, text. Everything from outside a program arrives as a string, and turning it into a number is a method that can fail. A price with a comma is the one that fails for a Brazilian user. By the end you can say the type of any expression, and what each conversion keeps.
